clue.text: Pal I shot in error might need its attention

definitions.text: Pal I shot in error might need its attention

indicators.note: done in error, the letters of these three words are wrongly placed and must be put right

explanation.surface: Someone who has accidentally shot a friend realises the victim will need medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in error' rearranges PALISHOT; the whole clue then describes where a friend shot by mistake would be taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A wounded friend would need the care of a medical institution with wards and doctors.

clue.text: Delay caused by an armed robbery

explanation.definitionFit: A hitch causing a wait in traffic or plans; also a robbery at gunpoint, as of a coach or bank.

clue.text: Soviet leader left in disgrace

indicators.note: the letter for left goes inside the word for disgrace

parts.note: a stain on one's character is a disgrace

explanation.surface: A Soviet leader is dropped in shame.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph, dictator of the USSR from the 1920s until 1953.

clue.text: To write from back to front in it is clumsy

indicators.note: the reversed word is placed inside the word it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: from back to front means the word for writing is read backwards

parts.note: to pen is to write

explanation.surface: A complaint that writing backwards is awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from back to front' turns PEN into NEP, which 'in' puts inside IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking skill or competence, awkward in handling things.

clue.text: Drives to a rendezvous on Sunday

indicators.note: on means the Sunday abbreviation is attached below, at the end in a down answer

parts.note: a venue is a meeting place

explanation.surface: Motoring to a meeting at the weekend.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad streets, often tree-lined; a drive is also a road name.

clue.text: Australian woman receives German greeting in South Africa

indicators.note: the greeting sits in the middle of the country's abbreviation, so one is placed inside the other

parts.note: Heil is the German salute or greeting

explanation.surface: An Australian woman is greeted in German while visiting South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for a girl or young woman.

clue.text: Once possessed sex appeal, but now over the hill!

parts.note: have had is the perfect tense of possess, owned in the past
it is a dated word for sex appeal

explanation.surface: An ageing beauty who has lost her allure.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being past one's prime, worn out or finished.

clue.text: For the alleviation of pain, it's outstanding

explanation.definitionFit: Given to ease suffering, as aid is sent; and standing out from a surface, as carving does.

clue.text: He gets held up by a parasite in the tavern

indicators.note: the man's word is held inside the phrase for a parasite, so it is placed within it

parts.note: a louse is a parasitic insect

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is written upwards, so its letters reverse

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man is detained by a scrounger in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns HE into EH, and 'gets held' puts that inside A LOUSE, after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a pub selling beer.

clue.text: Raised the dough to go away with Edward

parts.note: to leave is to go away
Ned is a familiar short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A baker's day: getting the bread to rise, then heading off with a friend called Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread dough is made to rise with yeast or another agent, which is the baking term here.

clue.text: Against a poem

parts.note: a verse is a poem or piece of poetry

explanation.surface: A protest written in rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Being opposed to something is having a strong dislike of it.

clue.text: Before climbing it, consult a vulcanologist!

definitions.text: Before climbing it, consult a vulcanologist!

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word is written upwards, so its letters reverse

parts.note: ante is Latin for before

explanation.surface: Advice to check with a volcano expert before going up the mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns ANTE upwards; the clue as a whole points to the Sicilian volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: The active volcano in Sicily, which a volcanologist would monitor.

clue.text: An investment which gives one confidence

parts.note: a unit is a single one
trust means confidence or faith

explanation.surface: A financial product sold as a source of reassurance.
explanation.definitionFit: A pooled fund in which savers buy units, a common British form of saving vehicle.

clue.text: Hail is sheer misery-nothing more

indicators.note: more says one further piece is added after the first

parts.note: hell is a state of utter misery
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A complaint that a hailstorm is pure torment.
explanation.definitionFit: To hail someone is to greet them, and this word is a greeting.

clue.text: In warfare soldiers once invoked his aid

definitions.text: In warfare soldiers once invoked his aid

indicators.note: the name sits in the run of letters spanning these two words

explanation.surface: Ancient soldiers prayed to a god for help in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is tucked inside 'warfare soldiers', and the clue as a whole describes the Greek god of war.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of war, whom fighters of antiquity called upon.

clue.text: Repeated it rapidly and staggered out

explanation.definitionFit: Recited a list quickly and fluently; and lurched unsteadily out of somewhere.

clue.text: Speak on modern wear

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the modern era of dates
dress is clothing, what one wears

explanation.surface: A talk given about contemporary fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak to a gathering is to give it a formal talk.

clue.text: Quick way to produce a crop

explanation.definitionFit: A quicker route; and a haircut that crops the hair close.

clue.text: Shows deference to a lady but not one's lady-love

definitions.text: Shows deference to a lady but not one's lady-love

parts.words: Shows deference to a lady but not one's lady-love
parts.note: a gentleman rises from his seat for a woman, yet the same phrase also means failing to turn up for a date with a sweetheart

explanation.surface: A man is courteous to women in general but treats his girlfriend badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Rises in respect; also jilts a date by not arriving.

clue.text: Rash fellow who obviously declined a sun-hat

explanation.surface: An impetuous man refuses protection from the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: An impulsive, quick-tempered person; and, read literally, someone with a sun-baked scalp from going bareheaded.

clue.text: Uppity boy consumes hot lentil puree

indicators.note: the boy swallows the letter for hot, which goes inside
uppity in a down clue reads the boy upwards, reversing it

parts.note: a lad is a boy
H stands for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: An arrogant boy eats a spicy lentil dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uppity' turns LAD into DAL, which 'consumes' H.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian dish of stewed split pulses, spelt also dal.

clue.text: Consider the cost

explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to judge or regard it; a rate is also a price or charge.

clue.text: Caesar crossed it to clean a church painting

parts.note: to rub something is to clean or polish it
an icon is a religious painting, as in Orthodox churches

explanation.surface: Restoring a church artwork, with a nod to Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: The river whose crossing by Julius Caesar began civil war in Rome.

clue.text: One beset by anxieties about tooth decay

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the letter for one sits inside the worries

parts.note: cares are worries
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone worried about a dental problem.
explanation.definitionFit: The dental term for decay or rot in a tooth.

clue.text: Class appears more scantily clad

explanation.definitionFit: A school period of teaching; and, split in two, wearing fewer clothes.

clue.text: Anger about US farm

indicators.note: about here means turned around or rearranged, so the word's letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Fury over an American ranch.
explanation.definitionFit: In the American West, an open area of grazing land for cattle.

clue.text: Breathe in orderly fashion and lie dormant

indicators.note: putting the letters in orderly fashion means sorting them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A relaxation instruction: breathe steadily, then rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' belongs to the fodder, not the indicator; 'orderly fashion' rearranges BREATHEIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that sleep through winter stay inactive for the cold months.

clue.text: Get up around noon to tint one's hair

indicators.note: the word for getting up goes around the letter for noon

parts.note: to rise is to get up

explanation.surface: Waking at midday to colour one's hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A temporary hair colouring, washed through the hair.

clue.text: Age cannot wither her, nor stale her infinite variety." (Antony and Cleopatra)

definitions.text: Age cannot wither her, nor stale her infinite variety." (Antony and Cleopatra)

parts.words: Age cannot wither her, nor stale her infinite variety." (Antony and Cleopatra)
parts.note: a quotation from Shakespeare with one word left out between nor and stale; the missing word is the answer

explanation.surface: Enobarbus's famous praise of Cleopatra's timeless charm.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank: the full line reads 'nor ... stale her infinite variety', with habit or usage as the missing word.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing noun means habit or established usage, which wears things out over time.

clue.text: Cast one's eyes over neckwear and lingerie

parts.note: to scan is to look over quickly
ties are worn round the neck

explanation.surface: Someone glances along a shop rail of ties and underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial word for women's skimpy knickers or underwear.

clue.text: Warning given to petty officer involved in an argument

indicators.note: the officer is caught up in the quarrel, so his letters go inside it

parts.note: a tiff is a minor quarrel
PO is the naval abbreviation for petty officer

explanation.surface: A naval NCO is cautioned after a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidential hint or advance alert passed on to someone.

clue.text: How retired agent thus appears in a pub?

definitions.text: How retired agent thus appears in a pub?

indicators.note: the agent and 'thus' are placed inside the pub word

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the agent word is read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales agent
so means thus

explanation.surface: A former salesman turns up at the local bar himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns REP into PER; with SO that goes inside INN after IN, and the whole clue describes turning up personally.
explanation.definitionFit: Being physically present oneself rather than acting through a representative.
